title: Preset filter searches names only — cannot find presets by script content
existing_state: The preset search box (InitializePresetSearchFilter, Form1.cs:8967-9037) filters via PresetMatchesFilter (Form1.cs:9080-9085), which is a single name-contains check: `presetName.Contains(filterText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`. FolderHasMatchingPresets (9087-9100) recurses folders but ultimately calls the same name-only predicate. In an app whose presets are multi-line YAML scripts and command lists, there is no way to answer "which preset touches `show running-config`?" or "where do I use the {{vlan}} variable?" — the user must open presets one by one.
recommendation: Extend PresetMatchesFilter to optionally match PresetInfo.Commands (the preset manager already holds all preset content in memory, so this is an extra string.Contains per preset — trivially fast at preset-list scale, and the 150 ms debounce at Form1.cs:9002 already protects against keystroke churn). Add a small scope toggle next to the filter box ("Aa | name+content") or a `c:` prefix convention, and visually distinguish content-only matches in the tree (e.g. dimmer star or suffix) so users understand why a preset whose name does not contain the term appears.
user_benefit: Content search is the expected behavior in every script-management tool (VS Code, SecureCRT command manager). For a user with dozens of YAML presets it is the difference between finding the right script in seconds versus opening them one at a time.

evidence.note: existing 150 ms debounce makes content scan cheap to add
